# Introduction

`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("iseeSpatial")` adds spatial panels to
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("iSEE")` for data at cellular resolution:
imaging-based (CosMx, Xenium) and sequencing-based (Visium HD,
cell-segmented). The data are a standard
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("SpatialExperiment")`.

A region selected on an overview map (fields of view for CosMx, single
cells for the other platforms) is applied to every panel: spatial plots,
quality-control histograms, spatial statistics, spatially variable genes,
cellular niches and spatial domains. Heavy analyses run only when the
user presses *Compute*, on the selected region.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("iseeSpatial")
```

# Example data

We use a small CosMx dataset shipped with
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("SpaceTrooper")`: one field of view (FOV) of a
tumour sample from the DBKERO database (https://kero.hgc.jp/), with 905
cells, about 1,000 genes, cell polygons and a cell-type label per cell.

```{r read}
library(iseeSpatial)
library(SpaceTrooper)

dir <- system.file("extdata", "CosMx_DBKero_Tiny", package = "SpaceTrooper")
spe <- readCosmxSPE(dirName = dir, sampleName = "DBKero")
spe
```

## Quality control

`spatialPerCellQC()` adds per-cell metrics (total counts, detected genes,
cell area in µm², distance to the FOV border, ...) and removes cells with
no counts. The cell polygons are then read and stored in `colData`; the
spatial panels draw them when *Use polygons* is ticked.

```{r qc}
spe <- spatialPerCellQC(spe)
spe <- readAndAddPolygonsToSPE(spe)
summary(spe$Area_um)
```

## Cell types and normalisation

The cell-type labels come with the example data. Negative-control probes
are removed before normalisation.

```{r labels}
labels <- read.delim(file.path(dir, "labels_tiny.tsv"))
spe$cell_type <- factor(labels$label[match(colnames(spe), labels$cell_id)])
sort(table(spe$cell_type), decreasing = TRUE)

spe <- spe[!grepl("^NegPrb", rownames(spe)), ]
spe <- scuttle::logNormCounts(spe)
```

The platform decides how a region is selected (FOV tiles for CosMx). It is
detected from characteristic `colData` columns or set explicitly:

```{r platform}
spe <- setPlatform(spe, "cosmx")
getPlatform(spe)
```

`load_cosmx()`, `load_xenium()` and `load_visiumhd()` (see
[Other platforms](#other-platforms)) give an object ready for the app in
one call.

# Niches and spatial domains

The spatial neighbour graph is built once (k nearest cells) and stored on
the object. **k is a choice**, not a constant: a small k describes direct
contacts, a large k a wider region. Pick it from the structures studied and
report it.

```{r graph}
spe <- buildSpatialGraph(spe, k = 15)
```

## Niches

A niche groups cells whose neighbourhoods have a similar cell-type
composition. `niche_entropy` measures how mixed each neighbourhood is
(0 = a single cell type).

```{r niches}
spe <- computeNiches(spe, label_col = "cell_type", k = 15, n_niches = 4)
table(spe$niche, spe$cell_type)[, c("BC cells", "CAFs", "TAMs", "Blood ECs")]
```

Each cell's neighbourhood composition is kept as a reduced dimension, so
one can ask, for example, what surrounds the tumour-associated
macrophages (TAMs):

```{r composition}
comp <- reducedDim(spe, "NicheComposition")
round(sort(colMeans(comp[spe$cell_type == "TAMs", ], na.rm = TRUE),
           decreasing = TRUE)[1:4], 2)
```

```{r niche-plot, fig.cap = "Niches of the example FOV.", fig.height = 5.5}
df <- data.frame(spatialCoords(spe), niche = spe$niche)
ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(CenterX_global_px, CenterY_global_px,
                                  colour = niche)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "x (px)", y = "y (px)") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    ggplot2::guides(colour = ggplot2::guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

## Spatial domains

Spatial domains cluster expression combined with the neighbourhood average
(`lambda` = weight of the neighbourhood; `lambda = 0` gives plain
expression clusters, also returned as `expr_cluster` for comparison). A
PCA is needed first.

```{r domains}
pca <- prcomp(t(as.matrix(logcounts(spe))), rank. = 15)
reducedDim(spe, "PCA") <- pca$x
spe <- computeSpatialDomains(spe, k_spatial = 15, lambda = 0.5,
                             resolution = 0.5)
table(domain = spe$spatial_domain, expression = spe$expr_cluster)
```

Niches and domains can be computed once on the whole dataset, as here, and
saved with the object; the app then shows them without recomputing, and
recomputes on a region only when asked.

# The app

## Analysis mode

```{r app}
app <- iseeSpatial(spe, mode = "analysis", cache = FALSE)
if (interactive()) shiny::runApp(app)
```

The analysis layout has:

* **Overview map**: the FOVs (CosMx) or cells; click or brush to select a
  region, *Clear* to go back to the whole dataset.
* **Two spatial plots**: coloured by cell type and by a gene; cells or
  polygons.
* **Spatial statistics**: global and local Moran's I of a gene
  (`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("Voyager")`), local cluster significance at a level
  set in the panel, join-count statistics and co-occurrence of the cell
  types, L-functions (`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("spatialFDA")`).
* **Spatially variable genes**: a ranking on the selected region; clicking
  a gene shows it in the linked spatial plot.
* **Niches / domains**: the results above, or recomputed on the selected
  region with *Compute*.

## QC mode

```{r app-qc}
app <- iseeSpatial(spe, mode = "qc", cache = FALSE)
```

Meant for unfiltered data: an overview map, a spatial plot of a QC metric,
QC histograms with outlier fences, and for CosMx an FOV zoom panel.

## Custom layouts

Panels can be combined freely, with each other and with any standard iSEE
panel, through `initial =`:

```{r custom}
panels <- list(
    SpatialMapPanel(),
    SpatialPlotPanel(ColorBy = "cell_type", UsePolygons = TRUE),
    SpatialQCPanel(Metric = "Area_um"),
    iSEE::ReducedDimensionPlot(Type = "PCA", ColorByColumnData = "niche",
                               ColorBy = "Column data"))
app <- iseeSpatial(spe, initial = panels, cache = FALSE)
```

## Image cache

Spatial plots are cached as images on disk (`spatialCacheDir()`), so going
back to a view already seen, or restarting the app, is instant. The cache
keeps 1 GB by default and drops the least recently used images first;
`cache = FALSE` keeps images in memory only (used in this vignette, so that
building it writes nothing to the user's folders) and `clearSpatialCache()`
empties the folder.

# Other platforms {#other-platforms}

```{r loaders, eval = FALSE}
spe <- load_cosmx("cosmx_spe.rds")                # a prepared CosMx object
spe <- load_xenium("path/to/xenium/outs")         # 10x Xenium bundle
spe <- load_visiumhd("path/to/segmented_outputs") # Visium HD, cell-segmented
```

Xenium and Visium HD data are selected cell by cell on the map. The full
Visium HD workflow of the OSTA book (QC, SingleR annotation, niches and
domains) is in
`system.file("scripts", "visiumhd_osta_workflow.R", package = "iseeSpatial")`.
